podcast.title: Early Music Involvement
podcast.body: Johnny began his musical journey in his early teens with his brother Colin, influenced by their older sister's interest in bands like George Evasion in the Fall. Initially, he attended "On a Friday" practices primarily because Colin was "babysitting him." However, after continuously expressing his desire to participate, he was eventually integrated into the band at approximately age 13, while the other members were 16 or 17. "after hearing him whine about wanting to do something, everybody just gave in and made him part of the band."

xref.title: First Recordings (1986)
xref.body: The earliest existing recording attributed to the band is a five-track cassette from 1986, which they self-issued at Abingdon. At this point, Johnny Greenwood was not yet a member, but a sax player named Razz Peterson was part of the lineup. The tape prominently featured 80s influences from bands like U2, Waterboys, Psychedelic Furs, and The Smiths, with Tom York handling lead vocals at 17 years old. "The earliest recording that seems to exist is a 1986 cassette that was recorded at Elbington."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hiatus for College (1991)
xref.body: In 1991, "On a Friday" entered an extended hiatus as all five members pursued higher education at different universities. Ed O'Brien went to Manchester University, Colin Greenwood studied English literature at Cambridge, Phil Selway also studied English literature at Liverpool University, and Johnny Greenwood enrolled in both music and psychology programs at Oxford. Tom York decided to take a year off before attending university. "In 1997, a 1991 on a Friday went on an extended sort of hiatus."

xref.title: Early Life and Music
xref.body: Colin, along with his younger brother Johnny, became involved in music during their early teenage years. Their interest was significantly influenced by an older sister who was keen on bands such as George Evasion in the Fall. "Thanks to an older sister who was in debates like George Evasion in the Fall, the two brothers Colin and Johnny Greenwood got into music together in their early teens."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Lineup and Instrumentation
xref.body: In its formative years as "On a Friday," the band's instrumentation was quite fluid and experimental. Johnny Greenwood, who joined around age 13, often played harmonica, recorder, and occasionally keyboards. At different points, the group featured "an all-female horn section" and even three saxophone players, despite acknowledging that the sax players "weren't very good, but at least they were having a good time." "Now at first, on a Friday was all over the place. Johnny played harmonica, sometimes the recorder, complete keyboards, every once in a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influences During Okay Computer Sessions
xref.body: During the recording of what would become "Okay Computer," Jonny Greenwood was heavily influenced by Pink Floyd, listening to their old albums and watching performance films. Tom Yorke, meanwhile, was entranced by old Johnny Cash records. "Johnny Greenwood was into a big pink void trip at the time, fortunate to listen to all these old albums and demanding that they watch old pink void performance films."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Joining Radiohead
xref.body: Johnny Greenwood, the youngest member, joined the band by consistently accompanying his older brother, Colin, until he was eventually integrated into the group. "he only made it into the band because he kept hanging around with his older brother, calling so much that he just was sort of folded into the group."

xref.title: Jonny Greenwood's Telecaster Plus
xref.body: Radiohead's Jonny Greenwood is a significant admirer of his Telecaster Plus, which features a maple neck and a distinctive sunburst finish. While the exact manufacturing date is not specified, its sound is highly regarded. "Johnny Greenwood is a huge fan of his Telecaster Plus with its maple neck and sunburst finish."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Story of the Electric Guitar - Part 3

xref.title: Multi-Instrumentalist and Composer
xref.body: While primarily a guitarist, Johnny Greenwood is proficient in piano, electronic instruments, viola, harmonica, banjo, and peculiar instruments like the Ondes Martenot and Indian Tampura. He has also developed a significant career as a composer for film, TV, and documentaries, working across rock, indie, jazz, chamber orchestra, and classical styles. "Not only has Johnny been a key element to the Radiohead sound, but he's also become quite the composer on his own, especially when it comes to soundtracks for movies, TV shows, and documentaries."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rejection of "Guitar Hero" Label
xref.body: Johnny Greenwood actively rejects the concept of a "guitar hero," viewing the guitar simply as a tool for making music, akin to a typewriter for writing or a vacuum cleaner for housework. "He also refuses to buy into this whole idea of the guitar hero. To him, guitars are just for making music, like a typewriter was used to write novels or a vacuum cleaner is used for housework."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
